scene: Scene 1: EXT. DEEP WITHIN THE RAINFOREST – DAY
text: Shot 1: Extreme wide, 18mm, slow crane down through canopy. Camera descends through layers of enormous tropical flowers — towering stems with soft swaying necks and luminous open petals heavy with golden pollen. Volumetric god rays pierce the canopy in shafts of warm amber, catching floating pollen motes. Foreground: massive dewy petals frame the shot in soft bokeh. Midground: two tiny buzzing shapes weave between flower stems — Fuzzby and Zenny, almost ant-scale against the botanical giants. Background: deep jungle layers recede into misty green-blue haze. Subsurface scattering glows through translucent petals as backlight hits them. The world feels ancient, alive, breathing. Tiny pollen sacks bounce visibly on both characters' back legs as they work.

scene: Scene 1: EXT. DEEP WITHIN THE RAINFOREST – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, tracking laterally. Zenny glides through frame right-to-left with balletic precision — smooth arcs between flowers, each dip into a blossom perfectly timed, pollen collected with effortless grace. Her wings catch rim light, iridescent edges glowing. Behind her in the midground, Fuzzby zig-zags chaotically, his flight path a drunken scribble compared to her clean lines. He hums visibly, whole body vibrating with enthusiasm. Warm dappled light filters through petals above. Ambient occlusion deepens the shadows in flower cups. The contrast between their two flight styles tells the entire relationship. FUZZBY: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, handheld with subtle drift. Fuzzby's face fills the frame as he dives nose-first into an enormous flower cup. Golden pollen ERUPTS around him like a dust explosion. He scoops wildly, overdoes it — his body spins sideways. Camera whip-pans as he clips a broad leaf — FWIP — bounces off it, tumbles, then catches himself mid-air. He straightens up, puffs out his tiny chest proudly. Pollen dust halos him in warm backlight. His eyes sparkle with oblivious confidence. Specular catchlights dance in his pupils. FUZZBY: Nailed it.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium close-up, 65mm, static. Zenny glides into frame beside Fuzzby, watching him with one eyebrow raised. She hovers with perfect stillness — a contrast to his wobbling. Beat. She studies him. Her expression shifts from assessment to reluctant amusement. Soft bounce light from a nearby yellow petal warms her face from below. Background: out-of-focus flower stems create vertical leading lines. She tries to keep a straight face. Fails slightly at the corner of her mouth. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 1: EXT. DEEP WITHIN THE RAINFOREST – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Fuzzby zooms to another flower and plunges his entire face deep into the pollen cup. Camera holds on the flower's rim — his tiny legs kick in the air. He pulls back out and his whole face is dusted thick yellow like an absurd fuzzy moustache. He blinks, delighted with himself, turning to present his look. Pollen particles drift off him in the warm crosslight. Zenny enters soft focus in the background, her shoulders shaking with suppressed laughter. FUZZBY: Do I look official?. Cut to. Shot 2: Two-shot, 50mm, locked off. Fuzzby faces Zenny proudly, pollen moustache prominent. He poses — chin up, tiny paws on hips. Zenny's composure cracks — she covers her mouth, eyes bright with laughter. The warm amber light catches pollen floating between them. Fuzzby gasps at her reaction and frantically wipes at his face with both paws, somehow smearing the pollen worse — it spreads across his forehead and cheeks. He looks like a tiny golden mess. Zenny's laugh finally escapes. ZENNY: Yes Fuzzby. Officially nuts!. Cut to. Shot 3: Wide shot, 35mm, slight low angle. Fuzzby launches toward another flower — clips a branch — tumbles end over end through the air, a tiny golden pinwheel. THUP. THUP. THUP. He crashes upside-down INTO a blossom, legs sticking straight up and kicking. Camera holds on the absurd image — two tiny legs waving from inside a pink flower cup. Beat of perfect comic stillness. Then he POPS back up like a cork, pollen exploding outward. Arms wide in triumph. God rays catch the pollen cloud around him like a tiny golden explosion. FUZZBY: Buzz Crash!!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 1: EXT. DEEP WITHIN THE RAINFOREST – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, gentle orbit. Zenny rolls her eyes but smiles warmly now — she has given up resisting. Fuzzby hums even LOUDER, vibrating with chaotic energy, and dives into yet another flower. Camera follows his arc. He pops back out somehow MORE covered in pollen than before — completely golden from head to toe, practically glowing. He hovers there, a fuzzy golden orb, utterly pleased with himself. Zenny watches him, fondness breaking through her composure. Soft warm light. Peaceful.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 28mm, static. Both characters hover in the warm air between flower stems. A moment of calm. Then — a distant RUMBLE rolls through the soundscape. The flowers shiver almost imperceptibly. Light shifts: warm amber dims slightly as if a cloud crossed the sun far away. Fuzzby freezes mid-hover. His wings slow. His expression shifts from joy to uncertainty. The pollen floating in the air seems to hang suspended. Something in the atmosphere has changed. Cool blue-grey begins to creep into the edges of the frame's color temperature.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Fuzzby's face — still dusted in pollen — registers the rumble. His eyes widen. One antenna twitches. He looks frame-left toward where the sound came from. The catchlights in his eyes dim slightly as the ambient light cools. His mouth opens — about to speak. The comedic energy drains into something more uncertain. Warm rim light still edges his golden-dusted silhouette, but the fill side of his face is cooler now. FUZZBY: …okay that sounded dramatic. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 1: EXT. DEEP WITHIN THE RAINFOREST – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 65mm, slight pan right. Zenny glances upward toward the canopy, then out through a gap in the trees toward the sky. The light has shifted — warmer tones retreating, replaced by a cooler steel-grey wash. Leaves high above them begin to tremble more noticeably. She reads the atmosphere with quiet intelligence. Her body language shifts subtly from relaxed to alert — wings angle slightly, posture straightens. She turns back to look at Fuzzby. Concern in her eyes but steady, not panicked. ZENNY: A Storm's coming.. Cut to. Shot 2: Two-shot, 50mm, static. Both hover side by side. Fuzzby looks to Zenny for confirmation. She nods once, certain. The forest around them has shifted — what was warm and golden is now cooling, shadows deepening between the flower stems. Wind picks up slightly — petals sway harder. A few loose pollen motes blow sideways through frame. The mood has turned. Zenny is already calculating their route back. Fuzzby is still processing.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Fuzzby — same framing as shot 9 setup. His expression shifts from worry to forced bravado. He puffs up slightly. His pollen-dusted face tries to project confidence. One eye twitches slightly. The cooling light makes the golden pollen on his face look less comical now and more like war paint. He speaks with exaggerated nonchalance, but his wings beat just a little faster than normal. FUZZBY: Good thing I work well under pressure. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 1: EXT. DEEP WITHIN THE RAINFOREST – DAY
text: Shot 1: Medium close-up, 65mm, static. Same framing as shot 10 for Zenny. She sighs — a full-body exhale that tilts her slightly in the air. Behind her, through the flower stems, we can see the sky darkening further through gaps in the canopy. She looks at Fuzzby — already knowing what is coming. Patient exasperation mixed with genuine care.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 35mm, slight push-in. Fuzzby immediately dives headfirst into another flower and gets STUCK again — legs kicking wildly from the blossom cup. The wind is picking up now, swaying the flower he is trapped in back and forth like a pendulum. Zenny hovers beside him, arms crossed. She waits. One beat. Two beats. The absurdity against the building atmospheric tension creates a perfect comic-dramatic contrast. Cool light continues to shift across the scene.. Cut to. Shot 3: Extreme wide, 18mm, crane up. Camera pulls back and rises through the canopy, revealing the vast rainforest stretching to the horizon. In the distance, dark storm clouds mass and roll toward us — enormous, ominous, bruise-purple and steel-grey. The tiny flowers where Fuzzby and Zenny work are barely visible far below, warm golden dots against the increasingly cool and threatening landscape. Lightning flickers silently inside the distant cloud bank. The scale shift — from intimate comedy to vast approaching danger — is breathtaking.

scene: Scene 2: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – AIDA'S SANCTUARY – DAY
text: Shot 1: Extreme wide, 18mm, slow push-in. A sheltered cove at the edge of the rainforest — turquoise water laps onto pale sand framed by weathered crystal formations that catch and refract light in soft prismatic patterns. Aida sits perfectly still in the center of a natural stone alcove near the waterline, cross-legged, tiny against the vast peaceful landscape. Beside her, a crystal singing bowl glows faintly. God rays angle down through high palm fronds. The entire scene breathes tranquility — soft ambient occlusion in the rock crevices, water caustics rippling across stone surfaces. The ocean's rhythm is the only movement.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium close-up, 85mm, locked off with imperceptible drift. Aida's paw moves the wand slowly around the crystal bowl's rim. The bowl resonates — a shimmering harmonic tone that seems to make the air itself vibrate. Extreme detail on the bowl's crystal surface: micro-scratches, translucent edges where light passes through with subsurface scattering. Her paw is steady, practiced, meditative. The wand traces a perfect circle. Water droplets on nearby stones tremble with the vibration. Warm golden fill light from the sand bounces up onto her face.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, very slow push-in. Aida closes her eyes. Her Rose Quartz pendant begins to glow — soft pink light rises from within the crystal, pulsing gently like a heartbeat. The pink luminance washes up across her face, her fur catching it in soft subsurface scatter along her ears and cheeks. Her expression is serene, focused inward. The background falls to deep soft bokeh — just shapes of water and light. The catchlights in her eyes (visible through nearly-closed lids) shift from warm amber to rose pink. Something is being seen.

scene: Scene 2: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – AIDA'S SANCTUARY – DAY
text: Shot 1: Medium wide, 35mm, dreamy soft focus. AIDA'S INNER VISION — everything shifts to a dreamlike quality: softer edges, warmer saturation, gentle lens bloom. A wooden pier stretches out over impossibly bright blue water. A small sailboat waits, rigging swaying gently. Keen stands beside his Mum — he checks the straps on his satchel with careful precision. Checks them again. Then one more time. His Mum watches him with a proud smile that cannot quite hide the worry in her eyes. Light is golden-hour warm, idealized. The image has the quality of a memory or a vision — slightly ethereal, borders softly vignetted in rose-pink.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, slow pull back. Same dreamy vision quality. Keen's paws tighten the satchel strap one final time. His Mum's paw enters frame and rests gently on his shoulder. Her fingers curl with love and reluctance. The satchel's buckle catches a glint of golden light. Then the image begins to dissolve — edges bleeding into soft pink, the rose quartz glow reclaiming the frame.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, static. Back to reality. The pink glow fades gently from Aida's face like a sunset dimming. Her eyes open — calm, knowing, certain. She places a paw over her heart. The Rose Quartz pendant's glow subsides to a faint inner shimmer. A soft smile crosses her face — not surprise, but recognition. She has seen what she expected to see. The bowl beside her has gone silent. The ambient sound of waves returns. Warm key light from frame right, cool ocean-reflected fill from frame left.

scene: Scene 2: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – AIDA'S SANCTUARY – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, static then gentle tilt up. Aida speaks softly — her words barely louder than the waves. Then she rises gracefully to her feet with fluid, unhurried movement. The crystal bowl's final harmonic fades into the sound of distant wind. Her silhouette reads clearly against the bright cove behind her — strong, purposeful, maternal. The pendant catches one last glint of light as she turns. AIDA: It's time.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 35mm, static. Aida walks purposefully away from the sanctuary alcove toward the treeline of the rainforest. Her figure moves through bands of light and shadow cast by overhanging palms. The crystal formations in the cove behind her continue to shimmer faintly. She does not look back. Her stride is certain. The forest ahead is deep green, layered with mist. Leading lines from the rock formations and shoreline converge on her small determined figure. A sense of momentum — something has been set in motion. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: Shot 1: Wide establishing, 24mm, static. A sun-drenched wooden pier extends out over crystal-clear tropical water. A neat little sailboat bobs at the dock, ropes creaking gently. The island behind is lush and green — a small paradise. Keen stands on the pier beside the boat, carefully loading supplies. His Mum stands a few paces back, watching. The composition places them small against the vast bright ocean — two figures on the edge of a big moment. Warm golden light bathes everything. Water caustics dance on the pier's underside. The sailboat's sail is furled, ready. This is departure.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, gentle tracking right. Keen arranges his supplies on the boat with meticulous care — a rolled map placed just so, the satchel positioned, the berry pouch tucked beside a folded blanket. He studies the arrangement. Adjusts the map. Moves the satchel an inch. Checks the berry pouch. His paws are precise, deliberate, slightly anxious in their thoroughness. Warm key light from the high sun catches the wooden deck. Each item reads clearly — the inventory of a young adventurer who prepared for everything he could think of.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium close-up, 65mm, static. Keen's Mum stands on the pier, arms gently clasped. Her smile is warm and proud but her eyes are glassy — the light catches moisture she is trying to hold back. She watches her son fuss over his supplies. Rim light from the ocean behind her edges her silhouette in bright white-gold. Background: the soft blur of the island's green hillside. She takes a breath. Speaks. Her voice is steady but there is a tremble underneath. KEEN'S MUM: Keen… are you sure you've got everything?. Cut to. Shot 2: Over-the-shoulder from Mum, 65mm, static. Keen looks up from his satchel. He pats it confidently — a gesture meant to reassure her as much as himself. Then he pauses. Checks one more pocket just in case, unable to help himself. His Mum's shoulder and ear are soft in the foreground frame-left. Keen's face shows determination layered over nervousness. Warm reflected light from the water dances on his fur. KEEN: I've got this, Mum.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium close-up, 65mm, static. Keen's Mum — same setup as shot 2 for her coverage. Her smile deepens despite herself at his pocket-checking. Then it wavers. Her eyes search his face. She speaks — the words come carefully, each one weighed. The pride and the worry coexist in her expression. A gentle breeze moves a strand of fur across her face. KEEN'S MUM: I know… it's just… this is a big step. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Keen looks out at the vast open water stretching to the horizon. He swallows visibly — his throat moves, his jaw tightens slightly. The ocean is enormous and he is small. But he sets his expression. Trying very hard to be brave. The water reflects in his eyes — endless blue possibility and endless blue uncertainty. Rim light catches the edges of his ears. He turns back to his Mum and speaks — invoking her own words back to her. KEEN: Like you said… it's part of growing up.. Cut to. Shot 2: Two-shot, 50mm, static. Both stand on the pier facing each other. The boat bobs gently behind Keen. A tender, weighted beat between them. His Mum nods softly at his words. Then she reaches into her bag. Her movements are slow, reverent. She draws out two worn wristbands — leather, weathered with age and love. She holds them in both paws like sacred objects. The light catches their worn texture. Keen sees them and goes absolutely still. Recognition. Meaning. The air between them changes.. Cut to. Shot 3: Extreme close-up, 100mm macro, locked off. The wristbands rest in Mum's open paws. Detail: the worn leather grain, tiny scratches from years of wear, the warmth of hands that once wore them. Subsurface scattering through Mum's paw pads — translucent pink where the backlight hits. The wristbands have weight — physical and emotional. They fill the frame. Everything else falls to deep bokeh. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, static. Keen's Mum speaks, her voice soft with memory. Her eyes are distant for a moment — seeing someone else, somewhere else. Then she refocuses on Keen. A single tear forms but does not fall. The catchlight in her eyes trembles. She holds the wristbands out toward him. Behind her, the ocean breeze moves the pier ropes gently. Warm light. Quiet devastation and quiet joy, simultaneously. KEEN'S MUM: Keen… it's time for you to have your father's wristbands. | KEEN'S MUM: I still feel him… every day.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Keen receives the wristbands into his own paws. He turns them over carefully — feeling their weight, their texture, their meaning. His expression softens from brave-face into something more vulnerable. More real. His thumbs trace the worn edges where his father's wrists once were. Light shifts across the leather surface. His eyes glisten. He does not look up yet. This moment is between him and the object in his hands.. Cut to. Shot 3: Extreme close-up, 100mm, locked off. Keen's paws slide the first wristband onto his left wrist. Then the second onto his right. They fit perfectly — as if they were always meant to be his. He turns his paws slowly, taking them in. The leather settles against his fur. Warm golden light catches the wristbands' surface. A perfect fit. A perfect inheritance. His fingers flex, feeling the new weight. KEEN'S MUM: Promise me you'll always wear them. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, static. Same Mum close-up setup. She reaches out and brushes a paw gently against Keen's cheek. Her touch is tender, lingering. She speaks — the most important thing she can say. Her eyes are full but her voice is steady now. The breeze catches her fur. Behind her, the world is soft bright bokeh. This is the last touch before he goes. KEEN'S MUM: Wherever you go… You'll never be alone.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, static. Same Keen close-up setup. He absorbs her words. A small, real smile forms — not performed, not brave-face, just genuine. He looks at her with all the love a child can hold. He speaks quietly. Then adds the softer line. His voice carries the weight of knowing this goodbye matters. KEEN: I promise. | KEEN: I won't be. I love you, Mum.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, static. Same Mum close-up. She responds. Her voice cracks on the last word but she smiles through it. The tear she has been holding finally traces down her cheek, catching the light like a tiny crystal. She is letting go and holding on at the same time. KEEN'S MUM: I love you… my brave boy. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 35mm, static then slow pan right. Keen climbs into the boat. He unties the rope from the pier cleat — his paws careful, practiced. He pushes off. The boat drifts gently away from the dock. The gap of water between boat and pier widens. His Mum lifts a paw and waves. Keen waves back, trying to look confident. Then the boat wobbles unexpectedly — he flails, arms pinwheeling, catches the mast. Steadies himself. Pretends that was intentional.. Cut to. Shot 2: Two-shot, 50mm telephoto compression. Distance between them now. Mum on the pier growing smaller, laughing through her tears. Keen in the boat trying to maintain dignity after the wobble. He calls back to her with exaggerated confidence. The telephoto lens compresses the distance — they feel close even as they separate. Warm light. The boat drifts further. Water sparkles between them. KEEN: Still got it!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 3: EXT. KEEN'S ISLAND – THE PIER – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, slight low angle from water level. SPLASH — a dolphin BURSTS from the water beside the boat. Keen startles, stumbles back, then immediately lights up with wonder and delight. The dolphin — Squeaky — arcs through the air in a shower of spray, sunlight catching every droplet. Keen leans over the side of the boat, eyes wide, mouth open in a huge grin. Water spray catches the light in rainbow refractions. The moment shifts from farewell melancholy to adventure excitement. KEEN: Whoa!. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium close-up, 65mm, gentle tracking. Keen leans over the boat's edge, animated and joyful. Squeaky pops up from the water, chatters. Keen nods enthusiastically as if understanding perfectly. The dolphin's wet skin catches specular highlights. Keen's face is pure delight — the nervousness of departure transformed by this new friendship. Behind them, the pier and his Mum grow smaller. Ahead: open water. The camera subtly reframes to show more ocean ahead than island behind. The journey has begun. KEEN: Hey there! | KEEN: Nice to meet you too. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 4: EXT. AT SEA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Extreme wide, 18mm, slow crane across. Endless blue ocean stretches to the horizon under a bright sky dotted with white clouds. Keen's tiny sailboat cuts a wake through the sparkling water — a speck of white against infinite blue. The scale is breathtaking: tiny character, vast world. Squeaky leaps alongside the boat in graceful arcs, spray catching sunlight. Water caustics pattern the hull. The boat's wake creates leading lines from foreground to the distant horizon. Freedom and vulnerability coexist in a single composition.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, tracking alongside. Keen sits at the helm of his little sailboat, trying to look like a seasoned sailor. His fur ruffles in the wind. He leans over the side — Squeaky pops up from the water, chittering. Keen greets him with natural warmth, like they have been friends forever. Water droplets on the boat's rail catch specular highlights. The sail billows cleanly behind Keen. Warm bright lighting. Happy energy. KEEN: Oh!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 4: EXT. AT SEA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, gentle sway matching boat motion. Keen nods at Squeaky's chattering as if it is perfectly comprehensible language. His expression is pure confident camaraderie. He speaks to the dolphin with the easy familiarity of naming a friend. Squeaky leaps high beside the boat in the background — a blur of grey and spray against the blue sky. Keen's eyes follow the leap, delighted. Sun-kissed warmth across his face. KEEN: Hi! I'm Keen! Nice to meet you, Squeaky!. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium wide, 35mm, static from boat. Squeaky leaps dramatically in a high arc — clearing the frame entirely, spray trailing like diamonds. Keen laughs, tracking the leap. Then he looks down at his map, unrolling it across his knees. His brow furrows slightly. He looks at the horizon. Looks back at the map. Turns his head. Looks at the horizon from a different angle. Uncertainty creeping in despite the beautiful day. The map flutters in the breeze.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Keen holds the map, studying it intently. He rotates it. Then rotates it again — now it is upside down. His expression shifts through stages: concentration, confusion, forced confidence, slight panic masked as more confidence. The map's edges flutter. Water reflections dance across his face from below. Behind him, soft focus clouds are starting to shift — the first hint that weather is changing. KEEN: Squeaky. Perfect. You really do sound squeaky. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 4: EXT. AT SEA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 28mm, dynamic slight low angle. A sudden gust of wind HITS — the sail FLAPS violently, CRACKING like a whip. The boat lurches hard to one side. Keen stumbles sideways across the deck, grabbing the mast with both paws. The map flaps wildly in his grip. The sky behind has darkened dramatically — clouds rolling in fast, bruise-colored and ominous. The color temperature shifts rapidly from warm gold to cool grey-blue. Water chops up. The mood turns on a dime. KEEN: Okay… so if this is north… then I am definitely going… …one of the directions.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium close-up, 65mm, handheld with storm sway. Rain begins — first scattered drops hitting Keen's face, then thickening to sheets. He tries desperately to hold the map while steering. The wind SNATCHES it from his paws — the map whips away into the grey air. Keen lunges, arms outstretched, fingers grasping. Misses. His face cycles through shock, disbelief, panic. The map becomes a pale flutter disappearing into the dark storm. Rain streams down his face. Volumetric rain streaks catch what little light remains. KEEN: No no no no—!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 4: EXT. AT SEA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in through rain. Keen stands frozen. Rainwater sloshes around his feet on the boat deck. The horizon has vanished behind sheets of grey. His breathing is visible — quick, shallow. Lightning flickers far away, illuminating his face in a brief blue-white flash. His eyes are wide. Truly lost. His paws grip the boat's edge — knuckles white. The wristbands on his arms catch the lightning flash. He closes his eyes. Breathes. Centers himself. His lips move — speaking to himself, finding ground. KEEN: Oh no… I'm lost!!! | KEEN: I've got this… I've got this…. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 35mm, dynamic angle from water level. Through the storm chaos — massive waves, driving rain, the small boat pitching violently — a familiar CLICKING sound. Squeaky bursts from the dark water beside the boat, leaping through the storm spray. He dips and reappears, insistently signaling in one direction with his nose. Keen's eyes open. He sees the dolphin. Hope flickers across his face despite the rain. Lightning illuminates them both — tiny figures against enormous storm waves. KEEN: Follow you?. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium shot, 50mm, handheld with storm energy. Keen looks at the rough water — massive, terrifying. Looks at Squeaky — determined, certain. A decision crystallizes on Keen's face. He nods. Grabs the tiller. He wrestles the small boat around to follow Squeaky's heading. The boat groans and creaks. Rain lashes sideways. But Keen's jaw is set now — no longer frozen but acting. Squeaky surges ahead through the dark water. Keen follows. The wristbands glow faintly — barely perceptible in the storm light. KEEN: Okay… lead on, Squeaky!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 5: EXT. RAINFOREST EDGE – CONTINUOUS
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 28mm, tracking fast through trees. Wind whips through the rainforest edge — leaves shiver violently, branches sway and bend. Fuzzby and Zenny fly quickly through the air between the trees, heading toward the coast. The light is grey-green, storm-filtered. Fuzzby is slightly ahead, still talking — his mouth moving rapidly, body animated even in flight. Zenny follows close behind, focused and efficient. Rain begins to spatter through the canopy. Leaves and debris blow across frame. The urgency is palpable. FUZZBY: I'm just saying, if this turns into a full storm situation, I am extremely—. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, sudden stop. Fuzzby freezes DEAD in mid-air — his entire body locks. His wings hold him motionless. His expression transforms from chatty to stunned. One tiny paw slowly rises and points frame-right. His eyes go WIDE — enormous, saucer-like, filling with alarm. The animation holds on this frozen moment — the comedy of his sudden stillness after his constant motion. Wind blows rain across his face but he does not blink. Behind him, Zenny nearly crashes into his back, pulling up short.. Cut to. Shot 3: Over-Fuzzby's-shoulder, 50mm, rack focus. Following Fuzzby's pointed paw — rack focus from his small arm in sharp foreground to the distant ocean visible through a gap in the wind-battered trees. There, tiny against the churning grey sea, a small boat rises and falls between massive waves. Barely visible. Desperately small. The rack focus makes the discovery visceral — from intimate scale to vast danger in one pull. Storm rain streaks across the frame. Lightning flickers on the horizon behind the boat. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 5: EXT. RAINFOREST EDGE – CONTINUOUS
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Two-shot, 50mm, static. Fuzzby and Zenny hover side by side at the tree line, looking out at the storm sea. Fuzzby's expression is pure alarm — eyes huge, paws clasped. Zenny's expression softens immediately into compassion and concern — her brow furrows, her head tilts. Wind buffets them both. Rain runs down their fur. The contrast between his panic and her focused empathy reads clearly in their silhouettes against the grey storm light. ZENNY: Fuzzby?. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Zenny's face — calm, certain, compassionate. She speaks two words with quiet gravity. Her eyes do not leave the distant boat. Rain runs in tiny rivulets down her face. The storm light is cool grey-blue but her expression carries warmth. A character who sees suffering and immediately wants to help. Behind her, trees thrash in the wind — soft focus chaos framing her stillness. ZENNY: Someone's in trouble.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Fuzzby SNAPS from concern into action mode — his expression shifts in a single frame from worried to DETERMINED. His eyes narrow. His tiny body tenses like a coiled spring. He opens his mouth wide and YELLS with everything he has. His whole body vibrates with the force of his shout. Rain flies off him. Pure comic urgency — a tiny creature with the heart of a lion and the volume of a foghorn. FUZZBY: BEARS! BEARS! EMERGENCY BEARS!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 5: EXT. RAINFOREST EDGE – CONTINUOUS
text: Shot 1: Wide shot, 28mm, tracking fast. Fuzzby BLASTS off toward the beach at maximum speed — a golden streak through the grey-green storm air. Immediately — BONK — he flies face-first into a branch. His body recoils, wobbles. He shakes his head violently, blinks, then rockets forward again without missing a beat. Determination overcoming coordination. Leaves and rain swirl in his wake. The animation pushes the impact comedy — full anticipation, hit, squash-and-stretch recovery, then right back to top speed.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, smooth tracking. Zenny follows in Fuzzby's chaotic wake — calm, focused, but moving faster now than we have seen her move before. She weaves cleanly through the same obstacles Fuzzby crashed through. Her flight path is a clean arc where his was a zigzag. She leans forward with purpose. Rain streams off her streamlined form. Behind her, the rainforest recedes. Ahead: the grey light of the open coastline. The chase toward help has begun.

scene: Scene 6: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – STORM BUILDING
text: Shot 1: Extreme wide, 18mm, slow push-in. Crystal Cove under darkening skies — dark storm clouds mass overhead, the water churns grey-green, wind moves through the coastal grasses in waves. The Crystal Bears stand together on the shoreline in a loose formation — Aida at the front, nearest the water. Howey, Misty, Luna, Sunny, Amie and others are arrayed behind her. They look out at the turbulent sea. The crystal formations along the cove catch whatever stormy light remains, refracting it in muted prismatic patterns. The mood is tense, expectant. These characters read as a team even in silhouette.

scene: Scene 6: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – STORM BUILDING
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, handheld with chaos energy. Fuzzby comes HURTLING into frame from the right — a golden blur moving way too fast. He tries to stop. Cannot. His tiny body pinballs off a large shell — BONK — ricochets past Howey who ducks — caroms off a piece of driftwood — loops in a tight spiral — and lands in a soggy heap on the wet sand. Beat. His body is a crumpled pile. One tiny paw lifts from the wreckage. Full Pixar physical comedy — each impact has squash, stretch, and follow-through.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, low angle from sand level. Fuzzby lies in his soggy heap, paw raised. Sand sticks to his wet fur. One eye is squished shut. He speaks with forced casual dignity. Nobody around him reacts — they have seen this before. Behind him, the other bears' legs are visible, unmoved. Rain spatters around him. The contrast between his attempted cool and his total wreckage is peak comedy. FUZZBY: I meant to do that.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium shot, 50mm, handheld. Fuzzby scrambles up to his feet, wild-eyed, sand-covered, completely frantic. His whole body vibrates with urgency. He gestures wildly toward the sea, trying to form words but too out of breath. His mouth opens and closes. His paws make shapes. He bends over double, gasping. The bears around him watch patiently. Rain picks up. Wind tugs at everyone's fur. Comic desperation. FUZZBY: BEARS! BEARS! There's someone out there and they're — they're — they're —. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 6: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – STORM BUILDING
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium close-up, 65mm, static. Zenny floats in behind Fuzzby — steady, composed, not a single hair out of place despite the storm. She delivers the information Fuzzby cannot, with calm precision. Two words. The contrast between her poise and Fuzzby's chaos is the joke and the characterization simultaneously. Storm-grey rim light edges her silhouette. Rain beads on her wings. ZENNY: In trouble.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Same Fuzzby close-up setup as shot 2. He points at Zenny gratefully — jabbing his paw toward her like she has just solved the greatest mystery. His eyes are enormous. He yells the confirmation with all his remaining breath. Relief and urgency combined. Rain runs down his face. His golden pollen dust from earlier has been completely washed away by the storm. FUZZBY: IN TROUBLE! YES! THAT!. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium wide, 35mm, slow dolly toward water's edge. Aida steps forward from the group. She moves to the very edge of the water. The wind stirs her fur gently but she is utterly still — the calm center of the storm. She looks out across the churning grey sea. Through the driving rain, we glimpse it with her: a tiny boat, impossibly small, rising and falling between dark waves far out. The composition places Aida in the foreground rule-of-thirds right, the tiny boat a speck at the convergence of the ocean's leading lines. Her Rose Quartz pendant catches a glimmer. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 6: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – STORM BUILDING
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Aida's face — calm certainty. She has been expecting this. Her eyes find the distant boat through the rain with the focus of someone who has already seen this moment. She speaks — two quiet words that carry absolute conviction. The storm rages around her but her expression does not waver. Rose-pink light begins to gather faintly at the edges of her pendant. Rain runs down her face like tears, but she is not crying. She is ready. AIDA: There he is.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 28mm, static. The bears all look out at the storm sea together. A row of small figures against the vast grey ocean. Concern and hope in their postures — leaning forward, paws clasped, ears perked. Aida turns back to face them. Her silhouette against the grey sea is commanding. She speaks with quiet authority. The group draws closer together instinctively. The crystal formations behind them begin to shimmer faintly. AIDA: Everyone — activate your crystal powers.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium shot, 50mm, orbit right slowly. CRYSTAL CALL SEQUENCE begins. Aida touches her Rose Quartz pendant with one paw. She speaks the activation words — her voice rises above the wind. The pendant GLOWS — warm rose-pink light blooms from within, washing across her face and chest. The light pushes back the storm's grey. Camera orbits slowly around her as the glow intensifies, revealing the other bears gathering closer behind her, their own crystals beginning to respond with faint answering glimmers of color. AIDA: With open heart and love so bright — Rose Quartz Crystal, shine your light!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 6: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – STORM BUILDING
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium close-up montage, 65mm, quick cuts between static frames. Each Crystal Bear touches their crystal one by one. Misty's crystal glows with its distinctive color — a pulse of light washes up her face. Luna's crystal activates — softer, cooler light. Howey's — warm and strong. Each activation is a beat: touch, glow, pulse. The light from each crystal reflects in the bearer's eyes. Rain continues but seems to matter less as the combined glow grows. Quick cuts but each held long enough to read the character's face.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, static. Zenny touches her crystal. It glows — her face illuminated. She looks upward slightly, connecting to something larger than herself. Her usual practical composure is elevated into something luminous. The crystal light reflects in the rain around her like tiny pink-and-blue fireflies. Beautiful.. Cut to. Shot 3: Wide shot, 28mm, pulling back slowly. All the bears stand together in the storm. They speak as one — voices rising together above the wind. Every crystal glows. The combined light is extraordinary — rose, blue, warm gold, cool silver — a constellation of color pushing back against the grey storm. The bears' silhouettes are rimmed in their individual crystal colors. The glow intensifies. ALL: With love and with light, together unite — Crystal Bears, shine your light!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 6: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE – STORM BUILDING
text: Shot 1: Extreme wide, 18mm, dramatic low angle. A BRILLIANT BURST of combined crystal light SHOOTS outward from the group — a beam of multicolored luminance that arcs out across the dark churning sea like a lighthouse beacon. It cuts through rain, through cloud-shadow, through the grey. The bears are small at the base of this extraordinary light — tiny sources of an enormous signal. The beam stretches toward the horizon, toward the tiny boat. Volumetric light rays scatter through the rain. The most visually spectacular moment yet.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, static. The bears watch the beam race outward across the water. Their faces are lit by the combined glow — warm and hopeful against the storm. Fuzzby's mouth hangs open in awe at what they have created together. Howey stands firm. Misty's eyes are bright with hope. Aida remains steady, her pendant still pulsing. Together. Waiting. Hoping.. Cut to. Shot 3: Extreme wide, 18mm, static. The beam of crystal light stretches across the dark storm sea — a line of warm color cutting the grey world in half. At its far end, barely visible: the tiny boat. The scale is overwhelming. The light reaches. The story pivots.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 28mm, dramatic angle through rain. The beam of crystal light cuts through the grey storm, reaching across the churning water. Keen's boat pitches in the massive waves. The multicolored light falls across his face and the boat's wet surfaces. Keen sees it — his head lifts, his body straightens. Through the driving rain, the light paints a warm streak across his dark, storm-drenched world. Hope enters the frame literally as color entering a grey composition. Water crashes over the bow. The light holds steady. KEEN: What is that…?. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in through rain. Keen's face — rain-streaked, exhausted, scared — transforms as the crystal light washes over him. His eyes widen. The warm multicolored glow reflects in his pupils, creating shifting catchlights. His mouth opens slightly. His expression is pure wonder — what IS that? The light pushes back the storm's cool grey-blue on his face. A moment of beauty in chaos.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium shot, 50mm, dynamic water-level angle. Squeaky suddenly CRIES OUT — a sharp, distressed chirping. Keen snaps his gaze downward. The dolphin thrashes at the surface beside the boat — a ragged DRIFT NET is tangled tightly around his tail, pulling him under. Each wave drags the net tighter. Squeaky's tail flails. The net's ropes are cruel against his smooth skin. Rain pounds the water's surface. The crystal light flickers across the terrible scene. Keen's expression shifts instantly from hope to horror. KEEN: Squeaky!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, handheld with storm motion. Keen's face — the decision takes less than a second. He looks at the monstrous waves. Looks down at Squeaky struggling. No hesitation crosses his features. His jaw sets. His eyes narrow with determination. His paws release the boat's edge. He does not think. He acts. His body coils to dive. The wristbands glow faintly on his arms. Rain lashes his face but he does not flinch.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 28mm, slight slow motion. Keen DIVES from the boat into the churning black water. His body arcs through the storm air — small, brave, silhouetted against a flash of lightning for one frozen instant. The splash is enormous relative to his size. The boat rocks violently in his wake. The crystal light from the shore catches the spray. He disappears beneath the surface. The boat bobs alone. KEEN: Hang on!. Cut to. Shot 3: INTERCUT — Medium shot, 50mm, static. SHORE: The Crystal Bears watch from the cove beach, tense and still. Fuzzby's mouth hangs open. They saw the dive. Howey reacts — disbelief and admiration warring on his face. The storm wind whips their fur. Crystal light still emanates from behind them, casting their shadows long toward the water. HOWEY: He jumped in?!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, static. SHORE: Aida watches with calm certainty — she is not panicked. Her expression carries quiet awe. She speaks softly, almost to herself. Pride in her voice. Her pendant still glows. Rain runs down her face but she is immovable. She saw what he did: he did not hesitate. That means everything. AIDA: He didn't think twice.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 28mm, underwater. UNDERWATER: Everything shifts to muffled blue-grey. Bubbles stream upward. Keen swims hard through swirling murky water, kicking with desperate energy. Ahead and below: Squeaky, the drift net wrapped cruelly tight around his tail, pulling him deeper. Shafts of storm-light penetrate from above in fractured columns. Debris floats in the current. The underwater world is beautiful and terrifying — deep blue shadows, pale shafts of light, the distant rumble of thunder transmitted through water. Keen reaches toward Squeaky.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium close-up, 65mm, underwater. Keen reaches Squeaky. His paws grab the drift net — thick, tangled, knotted rope that bites into the dolphin's tail. He PULLS. Nothing. The current shoves them both sideways — Keen slips, tumbles, reaches again. Squeaky thrashes weakly, exhausted. Bubbles stream from Keen's mouth. His fur ripples in the current. The net is impossibly tight. Desperate micro-actions: grab, pull, slip, grab again. KEEN: I've got you!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Extreme close-up, 100mm, underwater. Keen's paws on the net — straining, fingers whitening through fur. Then his eyes flick to his own arms — the wristbands. A faint glow begins inside them. Soft. Steady. Not the crystal beam from shore — something else. Something personal. Something inherited. The glow is warm amber against the cold blue-grey water. Keen's expression shifts from desperation to focus. He plants his feet against a submerged rock. Centers himself. The animation holds this beat — the gathering of will.. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, underwater. Keen's face — eyes closed, concentrating. His lips move silently. He speaks to himself underwater — words forming in bubbles. The wristbands' glow intensifies, casting warm amber light across his face, pushing back the cold blue. Squeaky watches him from the edge of frame — eye wide, trusting. A moment of stillness in the chaos. Keen opens his eyes. Resolved. KEEN: I've got this… I've got this…. Cut to. Shot 3: INTERCUT — Close-up, 85mm, static. SHORE: Aida's face, warm crystal glow on her features. She speaks gently — three words of absolute faith. Her pendant pulses in sync with something far away. She knows. She can feel it. Rain on her face, but her expression is serene. Connected to Keen across the distance. AIDA: He's not alone. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, underwater, dynamic. Keen grips the net with both paws. The wristbands BLAZE with amber light now. He PULLS. The net strains — fibers stretching, creaking underwater. Above them, visible through the churning surface, the shadow of a MASSIVE WAVE gathers — a dark ceiling of water building overhead. Keen looks up. Sees it. Looks at Squeaky beside him. Time is running out. KEEN: Come on…. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, underwater, slow push-in. Keen's face — raw determination. He speaks one word. Then braces. Plants his feet wider on the rock. Every muscle in his small body tenses. The wristbands burn with light. He speaks again — STRONGER. The word forms in a burst of bubbles. KEEN: COME ON!. Cut to. Shot 3: Extreme close-up, 100mm, underwater. Keen's paws YANK the net. SNAP — fibers tear, unravel, release. The net TEARS apart in a burst of frayed rope. In the SAME INSTANT the massive wave overhead CRASHES — the ceiling of water collapses. The world EXPLODES into white foam and chaotic motion. Keen is THROWN sideways — tumbling through bubbles and dark churning water. Disoriented. Spinning. The light from his wristbands strobes through the chaos like a beacon in fog. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium shot, 50mm, underwater, dynamic tracking. Keen tumbles through the turbulence — up is down, dark and light swap places. Then through the chaos he sees Squeaky — free, tail liberated, swimming toward him. Keen reaches out. Their connection re-establishes. Squeaky surges beneath Keen. Keen grabs the dolphin's dorsal fin. Squeaky ROCKETS upward toward the surface. The water brightens as they rise — grey becoming silver becoming white becoming —. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 28mm, dramatic low angle. They BURST from the surface in an EXPLOSION of water and light. Keen gasps, coughs, then LAUGHS — pure exhilarated relief. Water cascades off them. Storm light and crystal light combine. Squeaky chirps triumphantly. Keen clings to the dolphin's back, soaked and grinning. The boat is gone somewhere behind them. It does not matter. They are alive. They are free. KEEN: You got me!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 7: EXT. OUT AT SEA – STORM
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: INTERCUT — Medium wide, 35mm, static. SHORE POV: The Crystal Bears watch as a shape rises over the incoming waves. It is Keen — riding Squeaky on the crest of a wave, silhouetted against the grey sky with the crystal light behind them. Howey's jaw drops. Misty claps a paw over her mouth. Sunny speaks — awe in his voice. SUNNY: The bravest guy I've ever seen. | MISTY: His boat's gone!!. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. SHORE: Fuzzby's face — pure awestruck wonder. His eyes are enormous, reflecting the approaching riders. Rain runs down his face but he does not notice. He speaks in a hushed, reverent whisper — the most sincere thing he has ever said. This tiny chaotic bee looking at this brave bear like he is witnessing a miracle. FUZZBY: When I grow up… I wanna be like him.. Cut to. Shot 3: Wide shot, 28mm, tracking alongside. Keen rides Squeaky over a wave like a tiny cowboy — one paw in the air, leaning back, a huge grin splitting his face. He YELLS with pure joy. The wave curls behind them. Storm spray catches what crystal light remains. Despite everything — the storm, the near-drowning, the lost boat — this is the most alive he has ever felt. The bears on shore are visible now, growing larger. Home ahead. The ride of a lifetime. KEEN: YEEHAW!!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 8: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 28mm, tracking alongside as they approach shore. Squeaky glides into the shallows — the water brightens from storm-grey to turquoise as they reach the cove's shelter. Keen hops off the dolphin's back into ankle-deep water, stumbling forward through the surf. He is laughing — breathless, soaked head to toe, fur plastered flat, but utterly exhilarated. He splashes through the shallows toward the beach. The Crystal Bears are visible on the shore ahead, gathered and waiting. Storm clouds break behind them, first shafts of golden light cutting through. KEEN: Best… ride… ever!. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, slight low angle. Keen reaches the sand. His legs wobble like rubber — the adrenaline draining. He nearly topples. Howey steps forward instinctively and catches him, steadying him with a firm gentle paw. Keen looks up at Howey gratefully. The other bears gather around them in a warm, protective circle — curious, gentle, smiling faces. Sunny bounces on his toes. Amie beams. The warm circle of bodies and faces creates a visual embrace before anyone has physically hugged.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Keen looks around at all of them — these faces he has never seen before but that feel immediately safe. Water drips from his fur. His eyes are bright despite the exhaustion. He introduces himself — simple, direct, genuine. The catchlights in his eyes are warm now — reflecting the faces around him and the first break of golden light through the clouds. A small, shy smile. KEEN: Hi… I'm Keen. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 8: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium close-up, 65mm, handheld with comic energy. Fuzzby ZOOMS directly into Keen's face — filling the frame — practically nose-to-nose. His eyes are enormous with excitement. He speaks with rapid-fire intensity, barely pausing between words. Keen leans back slightly, startled by this tiny golden ball of energy an inch from his nose. Fuzzby's wings blur. His whole body vibrates with excitement. Behind him, the other bears watch with amused familiarity — they know Fuzzby. FUZZBY: You rode a dolphin. Into a storm. On purpose?!. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, static. Keen blinks at the tiny bee creature in his face. Processes the question. His response is modest, uncertain, almost confused. He is still processing riding a dolphin through a storm. The comedy is in the understatement. Water drips from one ear. KEEN: …kind of?. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium shot, 50mm, static. Fuzzby slowly — dramatically — turns to the other bears. He raises one tiny paw and POINTS at Keen like a prosecutor presenting evidence. His expression is deadly serious. He speaks with the gravity of making a historic announcement. Beat. The other bears try not to laugh. Fuzzby is completely sincere. FUZZBY: He's amazing. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 8: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 65mm, gentle. Zenny floats in calmly and gently catches one of Fuzzby's legs, pulling him back from Keen's personal space with practiced ease. She speaks softly — two words. Fuzzby allows himself to be tugged but does not take his eyes off Keen. Zenny's expression is warm, patient, fond — she has been managing Fuzzby's enthusiasm for a long time. The interaction reads as a double act — comedy partners who know each other's rhythms perfectly. ZENNY: Give him space.. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 35mm, slight crane up. All the Crystal Bears together with Keen — a group shot. They speak in unison, welcoming him. The moment is warm, genuine, communal. Golden light breaks more fully through the clouds now, warming the beach. The crystal formations around the cove catch the new light and begin to shimmer. The bears' fur catches rim light. Keen stands among them — smaller than some, taller than others, but fitting in. Belonging. ALL: Welcome to Crystal Cove! We're the Crystal Bears!. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 8: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium close-up, 65mm, slow pan. Keen turns and takes in the cove — really SEEING it for the first time now that the crisis has passed. Glowing crystal formations. Warm golden sand. Gentle waves. Lush tropical vegetation. His expression opens into pure wonder. His eyes track across the landscape. Each detail registers. This place is magical. His mouth opens slightly. The camera pans with his gaze, revealing the beauty of Crystal Cove through his fresh eyes. KEEN: Wow… this place…. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 35mm, static. Keen turns back toward the sea. In the shallows, Squeaky leaps one final time — a graceful arc against the clearing sky. Water spray catches the new golden light like scattered diamonds. Keen watches him with gratitude and farewell. Aida steps forward beside Keen. She lifts a paw and makes a small, gentle gesture toward the dolphin. Squeaky watches her, seems to understand, dips his head once. Then dives beneath the waves. The surface settles. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 8: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Two-shot, 50mm, static. Keen looks at Aida — questioning, curious. Aida smiles — knowing, warm. She speaks. The revelation is gentle but lands with emotional weight — she has already thought of his Mum, already acted to ease that worry. Keen absorbs this. His expression moves through surprise, understanding, gratitude. A long moment. AIDA: Just getting a message home to your Mum. To let her know you're okay. | KEEN: What did you do?. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Keen's face — a soft, grateful pause. He says one word that carries everything. Two syllables weighted with exhaustion, relief, wonder, gratitude, and the beginning of belonging. His eyes are full. The warm light catches the moisture there without tipping into tears. Behind him, the Crystal Cove glows in the breaking golden light. He has arrived. KEEN: Thank you. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 9: EXT. GATHERING AREA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Extreme wide, 18mm, slow push-in. The storm has passed completely. The gathering area is a natural amphitheater in the forest near the cove — ringed by crystalline formations and lush vegetation. Everything glows fresh and washed clean. Water droplets cling to every leaf and crystal surface, catching the new sunlight in a thousand tiny sparkles. The Crystal Bears gather in a quiet circle. Aida and Keen stand at the center. The golden light is warm, clean, almost sacred. God rays angle through gaps in the canopy above. This is a ceremony space. The air feels charged with possibility.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium two-shot, 50mm, static. Aida and Keen face each other at the center of the circle. Keen still wears his father's wristbands — prominent on his wrists. Aida looks at him with warmth and certainty — maternal, wise, welcoming. Keen looks back — still a little awed, a little uncertain, but standing taller than when he arrived. Water droplets sparkle in both their fur. The circle of bears is visible in the background, soft focus, watching. Aida speaks — her words measured, significant. AIDA: You followed your heart… and chose courage. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 9: EXT. GATHERING AREA – DAY
text: Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, very slow push-in. The air between Aida and Keen begins to shimmer. A gentle AQUAMARINE LIGHT materializes — first as a faint glow, then brighter, coalescing into a shape. A glowing crystal appears, hovering in mid-air. Keen stares in absolute wonder — mouth open, eyes reflecting the aquamarine luminance. The crystal rotates slowly, humming with a soft harmonic tone. Subsurface scattering makes the crystal seem to glow from within. Keen's face is bathed in aquamarine light. Water droplets in the air around the crystal catch its glow like tiny blue-green fireflies.. Cut to. Shot 2: Extreme close-up, 100mm, locked off. The aquamarine crystal hovers, humming — then SPLITS into two smaller gems with a soft musical chime. The split is beautiful — organic, like a cell dividing, trailing threads of light between the two halves. The two smaller crystals orient themselves and begin to drift apart, moving with purpose. The detail is extraordinary: internal facets, captured light, the blue-green depth. Each gem pulses with a heartbeat rhythm.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, tracking down to wrists. The two aquamarine gems float toward Keen's wrists — toward his father's wristbands. They settle into place — one in each band — PERFECTLY. As if the wristbands were always meant to hold them. As if this was always the plan. A pulse of AZURE LIGHT runs through the wristbands — traveling from the crystals through the leather, illuminating the worn grain, the scratches, the history. Keen feels it — his whole body responds to the energy. His fingers spread, absorbing the warmth. The inheritance is complete.

scene: Scene 9: EXT. GATHERING AREA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Medium close-up, 65mm, slow crane up. Keen lifts his paws — amazed. The wristbands glow with steady aquamarine light. The light reflects in his eyes, his fur, the water droplets on his face. He looks at his paws like they belong to someone new. Then he speaks — his voice rising with each phrase, confidence building as the crystal responds to his words. The activation phrase comes out strong, clear, real. The light intensifies with each word. By the final word, he is luminous. KEEN: Brave and bright, with all my might — Aquamarine Crystal, shine with light!. Cut to. Shot 2: Wide shot, 28mm, static. The full ceremony circle — all bears watching. Keen stands at the center, wristbands blazing with aquamarine light, transformed. Fuzzby claps — too early, by himself. He stops. Looks around. Nobody else is clapping yet. Beat. Then he starts again, LOUDER, trying to make it seem intentional. Howey cheers. Misty beams. Luna smiles softly. The comedy and the triumph coexist perfectly. The circle of warm faces and crystal light. A coronation and a comedy in the same frame. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 9: EXT. GATHERING AREA – DAY
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 35mm, dynamic handheld. The whole group SURGES in and SWAMPS Keen in a giant bear hug. A chaotic, warm, joyful pile of bodies. Arms, paws, fur, squished faces, laughter. Keen is startled — his eyes go wide, arms pinned. Then he MELTS into it. His eyes close. He hugs back. Fuzzby is somewhere in the pile, probably squished. Zenny is at the edge, participating with dignity. The light from multiple crystals creates a warm glow around the group hug. This is family.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, gentle pullback. The group slowly breaks apart. Bears step back, smiling, wiping eyes. Keen looks around at all of them. His expression has changed — no longer lost, no longer alone, no longer trying to be brave. Just… home. Aida speaks — her words settling over the moment like a blessing. The warm light holds. The forest sparkles around them. Everything is as it should be. AIDA: Wherever you go… You'll never be alone.. Cut to. Shot 3: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Keen's face — a full, real, homecoming smile. Not performed. Not brave. Just genuine, deep, complete happiness. The aquamarine glow from his wristbands reflects softly upward onto his jaw. The catchlights in his eyes hold the warm shapes of the bears around him. He has found where he belongs. The camera holds on this face — letting the audience feel everything he feels. A long, warm, earned beat. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 10: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – CONTINUOUS
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Wide shot, 28mm, slow tracking alongside. The mood has lifted completely. Warm golden light bathes Crystal Cove beach. Gentle waves lap at the shore, leaving lace patterns in the wet sand. Keen walks along the beach with the Crystal Bears — a group of friends now, not strangers. The crystal formations along the cove sparkle in the afternoon light. Keen's aquamarine wristbands glow softly as he walks. The forest behind them is washed clean, vibrant green. Everything gleams. The composition is wide, warm, inclusive — a community walking together.. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium two-shot, 50mm, walking pace tracking. Fuzzby buzzes up beside Keen, hovering at shoulder height. He adopts a suddenly very serious expression — straightening his tiny body, composing his face. This is clearly important to him. His wings slow to a deliberate, measured beat. He speaks with exaggerated gravity. Keen glances at him, still catching his breath from everything that has happened. The contrast between Fuzzby's forced seriousness and his inherent goofiness is immediate. FUZZBY: So… quick question. | KEEN: Yeah?. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 10: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – CONTINUOUS
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 85mm, static. Keen's face — he considers the question genuinely. He answers simply, honestly. Beat. Fuzzby GASPS beside him — the reaction is visible even in Keen's frame as the tiny golden blur beside him goes rigid with excitement. Keen's expression shifts to amused confusion. The warm beach light catches his face. His wristbands glow in the lower edge of frame. FUZZBY: How do you feel about honey? | KEEN: Uh… I like it?. Cut to. Shot 2: Close-up, 85mm, locked off. Fuzzby's face — PURE ECSTASY. His eyes SPARKLE. His mouth trembles with joy. This is genuinely the greatest news he has ever received. His reaction is pushed to maximum Pixar expression — eyes impossibly wide, tiny paws clasped to his chest, wings vibrating at a frequency that suggests he might explode. He speaks with reverent intensity. The golden beach light makes his pollen-free fur glow. This friendship is destiny. FUZZBY: Oh… this is going to work out VERY well.. Cut to. Shot 3: Medium shot, 50mm, static. Zenny appears in frame, calm as always. She speaks — a gentle warning, a habitual redirect. But Fuzzby is already gone — buzzing in excited circles around Keen, who watches this tiny golden tornado orbit him with growing delight. Keen turns to follow Fuzzby's orbit, getting slightly dizzy. Zenny watches them both with fond exasperation. ZENNY: Fuzzby…. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera. After the final line they HOLD the look, about 2 seconds of silence, no more dialogue.

scene: Scene 10: EXT. CRYSTAL COVE BEACH – CONTINUOUS
text: ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Shot 1: Close-up, 65mm, handheld tracking with Fuzzby's orbit. Fuzzby circles Keen, listing honey-related activities at machine-gun speed. Each item is punctuated with a gesture — miming eating, napping, drizzling. His enthusiasm is BOUNDLESS. Keen laughs — a real, free, joyful laugh. The kind he has not had since before the storm. Warm light. Warm friendship. Pure comedy. FUZZBY: Honey cakes, honey snacks, honey naps, honey leaf drizzles, emergency honey—. Cut to. Shot 2: Medium shot, 50mm, gentle. Zenny catches one of Fuzzby's legs again — mid-orbit — and pulls him to a gentle stop. She speaks with patient precision. Fuzzby hangs in the air, held by one leg, still talking, still gesturing. He responds with his whole heart. Keen watches them — this double act, these instant friends — and laughs harder. The bears continue walking along the beach together. ZENNY: One thing at a time. | FUZZBY: I have waited my whole life for this friendship!. Cut to. Shot 3: Extreme wide, 18mm, slow crane up and pullback. Camera rises as the group walks together along the golden beach — Keen at the center, Fuzzby buzzing around him, Zenny gliding alongside, the other bears visible further along the shore. The cove stretches out behind them — crystal formations sparkling, turquoise water gentle, palm trees swaying in a warm breeze. The storm is a distant memory. The light is perfect golden-hour warmth. As the camera pulls back and rises, the full beauty of Crystal Cove reveals itself — a paradise, a home, a beginning. The figures grow small but never alone. The ocean stretches to the horizon. The crystals glow. Everything ahead is possibility. Characters look across the frame at each other, NOT at the camera.
